activationNote: IMPORTANT, verified by direct code inspection of scripts/verify-control-dependencies.mjs's baseCheckerPinBumpErrors: this record's controlGatePinBump would need to be embedded, verbatim, inside product/dependency-verification.json AT the exact commit that CI checks out as the PR/push head (candidateTree). But candidatePinsSha256 above only covers product/dependency-pins.json's bytes, NOT this file -- so that part IS stable and reusable. candidateTree, however, is the full commit SHA of whatever the actual PR head is at CI time. The commit that adds this signed record necessarily changes that commit's own tree (this file is part of it), which changes its own resulting SHA -- so a commit cannot correctly state its own SHA inside itself; this is not a bug to work around, it is a property of cryptographic hashing (finding a fixed point of a SHA-based commit hash is computationally infeasible, not merely inconvenient). Two real ways forward, neither of which is 'A embeds this and hopes': (1) The owner reviews this exact diff (six digests above, against candidateTree 3fd6085b1319f1b4e767bbaead8f13b94c6e1298 or whatever later commit is the true final one) via GitHub's own PR review, and merges using their repository-admin ruleset bypass privilege for this one verified merge, instead of trying to satisfy this specific automated check -- GitHub rulesets support designated bypass actors for exactly this kind of owner-reviewed exception, and doing so requires no code change and no fabricated approval object. (2) If the in-repo mechanism must be used, someone with commit access creates ONE additional commit whose only change is adding this file with candidateTree left temporarily blank, learns that commit's real SHA via `git rev-parse HEAD`, and accepts that a strict-equality check against that exact value will still fail on THAT commit (by construction) -- meaning this mechanism as currently written cannot self-validate its own activation commit for ANY candidate, ever, not just this one. That is a design gap in scripts/verify-control-dependencies.mjs itself, owned by A, and is reported as such rather than silently worked around.
recommendedResolution: Use option (1): owner reviews and merges via the ruleset's bypass mechanism for this specific, verified candidate. Do not ask A to embed a self-referential candidateTree; it cannot be done correctly. A did not and will not set approvalToken to "OWNER APPROVED" itself.
